questions.text: Three processes arrive at time zero with CPU bursts of 16, 20 and 10 milliseconds. If the scheduler has prior knowledge about the length of the CPU bursts, the minimum achievable average waiting time for these three processes in a non-preemptive scheduler (rounded to nearest integer) is _____________ milliseconds.
questions.solution:
Shortest job first minimizes average waiting time. Order 10, 16, 20:
waiting times 0, 10, 26 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average = 36 / 3 = 12 ms.

Answer: 12

questions.text: Which of the following standard C library functions will always invoke a system call when executed from a single-threaded process in a UNIX/Linux operating system?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- exit: must ask the kernel to end the process [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always a system call.
- sleep: must ask the kernel to suspend the process [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always a system call.
- malloc: often served from already allocated heap memory; calls brk/mmap only sometimes.
- strlen: pure user-space computation.

Answer: exit, sleep

questions.text: In the context of operating systems, which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to paging?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Any free frame can hold any page, so there is no external fragmentation [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Larger pages waste more space in the last page (internal fragmentation) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Page tables take memory (and TLB, extra accesses) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Multi-level paging is used to shrink page tables, not to support different page sizes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Options 1 and 3

questions.text: The hardware implementation which provides mutual exclusion is
questions.solution:
Test-and-set is an atomic hardware instruction that can directly build a lock. Semaphores are a software (OS) mechanism, often built on top of such instructions.

Answer: Test and set instructions

questions.text: Three CPU-bound tasks, with execution times of 15, 12 and 5 time units respectively arrive at times 0, t and 8, respectively. If the operating system implements a shortest remaining time first scheduling algorithm, what should be the value of t to have 4 context switches? Ignore the context switches at time 0 and at the end.
questions.solution:
Tasks: A (15, at 0), B (12, at t), C (5, at 8). Four switches need two preemptions:
- B must preempt A at t: [latex]12 \lt 15-t\Rightarrow t \lt 3[/latex] (switch 1).
- C must preempt B at 8: B's remaining time [latex]12-(8-t)=4+t \gt 5\Rightarrow t \gt 1[/latex] (switch 2).
- C finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B (switch 3) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A (switch 4).

So t must be between 1 and 3. Among the options, 0 [latex]\lt[/latex] t [latex]\lt[/latex] 3 is the only one covering this range.

Answer: 0 [latex]\lt[/latex] t [latex]\lt[/latex] 3
